failures.criterion: AC10 — every text the change makes false is true at the head. `skills/envoy/SKILL.md:136-142`, the paragraph this pull request rewrites, is false at the head, and the contrast it newly draws is the opposite of what the code does.
failures.evidence: The shipped text reads: `Your own envoy_publish to a role or to a built-in topic never reaches the agent that spawned you. The listener delivers nothing to the session a message names as its source, and inside a subagent that source is your parent, so a publish to a role it holds, or to a GitHub, Dispatch, Slack or other built-in topic it subscribes to, is accepted and delivered to nobody. Use a write to its agent:// address for that one hop. A team topic (below) is the exception: it travels live over NATS, which has no such skip, so it reaches your parent, and your own session too when it subscribes.` Driven on the live surface, in this pod, against the deployed listener (ENVOY_URL, the old build — this is not behaviour the change introduces): this session subscribed with `envoy_subscribe` to `notifications.github.infra113tester.probe.>` (the listener answered `Subscribed: notifications.github.infra113tester.probe, notifications.github.infra113tester.probe.>`), a stream-captured built-in GitHub topic. A `task` subagent of this session then published to `notifications.github.infra113tester.probe.pr.1.comment` with `envoy_publish` and got back `published d6e2bcf056032b9b9eb53dc20d4ba6f6`; that is exactly the documented scenario, a subagent's publish whose source is its parent. The parent — this session — received it: the Envoy delivery arrived in this transcript as `from: 01a1624f-7d82-76c7-a978-0bf32a39476f (Legion tester · INFRA-113), id: d6e2bcf056032b9b9eb53dc20d4ba6f6`. A direct publish from this session to the same topic arrived the same way (`published 2dd05898275b91d9de0a7b506a290f96`, delivered as id 2dd05898275b91d9de0a7b506a290f96). So a built-in topic is not 'delivered to nobody', and the team topic is not 'the exception'. The code says why, and no test contradicts it: pi-envoy registers every session `selfSubscribed: true` with `port: 0` (packages/pi-envoy/extensions/envoy.ts:1500-1517) and holds its own NATS subscription per topic, expanded to both `<base>` and `<base>.>` (packages/envoy-client/src/transport.ts:114-132, used at extensions/envoy.ts:1238-1248); the listener skips its push entirely for a self-subscribed session with no port (packages/envoy/internal/session/session.go:62), so the fanout's source skip (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/delivery.go:638, `listener skip echo`) never reaches it; and a JetStream publish is a publish on the subject, so a core subscriber of a captured subject is handed it — measured in the rig at this head, where the credential-free subscriber RECEIVED `notifications.github.probe.all` (AC2) exactly as it RECEIVED the ad-hoc topic. The real distinction is the listener's push path (a session with a port, such as the OpenCode plugin, which `packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:2193-2201` states correctly for ad-hoc topics) and the role lane's holder resolution — not built-in versus team topic. No red test is committed for this one: the defect is in shipped prose, and a test over wording is the kind this repository's rules forbid; the behaviour the prose misstates is already correct and already covered by `TestPublishHandlerDeliversAnAdHocTopicToItsSubscriber` (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main_test.go:377) in CI's envoy-go. Fix is the sentence: say that the listener's own push is what skips the source, that a session holding its own NATS subscription (every Oh My Pi session) receives its own publish on any topic it subscribes to, built-in topics included, and that the `agent://` hop is needed only where the listener's push is the delivery path. The same care applies to the comment at packages/pi-envoy/extensions/envoy.ts:2925-2932, which is narrowly true of the listener ('the listener never delivers…') but reads as the same false contrast; it is the place the role-only `undelivered` flag is explained, so it wants one clause saying the session's own NATS subscription is unaffected.

observations: A wildcard topic is accepted rather than refused: `notifications.>` and `notifications.*.probe` answer 200 and are published as literal subjects, reaching only a subscriber whose own subscription is a wildcard at that level (a catch-all `notifications.>` subscriber received the literal `notifications.>` message; the concrete subscribers did not). It reaches no agent subject — `notifications.agent.>` is refused by the agent-topic check, the stream captured none of these (ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS stayed at 0 messages), and the listener's role-lane queue subscription does not match them. This is not new in kind (a wildcard under a captured prefix was already publishable and retained before this change) and no shipped text claims otherwise, so it is recorded rather than filed: a publish restriction to literal subjects would be its own issue.

`notifications.AGENT.s1` answers 200 because the agent-topic refusal is case-sensitive, as NATS subjects are; it reaches no subscriber of `notifications.agent.s1`. Unchanged by this PR and harmless, recorded for completeness.

The `<subject>.>` subscription that `skills/envoy/SKILL.md`'s Team topics section tells a group to use does cover the bare `<subject>` the CHANGELOG and AGENTS.md examples publish to, because the client subscribes both (packages/envoy-client/src/transport.ts:114-132). Checked because a core-NATS `x.>` subscription alone would not match `x`, and the listener does no expansion on the core path.
